1.

2. Heard Sri Vinod Kumar Shukla, learned counsel for the applicant and Smt. Vatsala, learned counsel for the informant as well as Sri Yogesh Mishra, learned A.G.A. for the State and also perused the record.

3. The present application for anticipatory bail has been filed for protection in regard to FIR/Case Crime No. 60 of 2023, under Sections 419, 420, 467, 468, 471, 406, 504 of I.P.C., P.S.- George Town, District- Prayagraj.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, reported in 2022 SCC Online SC 825
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5. Learned counsel for the informant as well as learned AGA have no objection to the prayer made by the learned counsel for the applicant.
6.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties, no case is made out for interference u/s 438 Cr.P.C..

The present anticipatory bail application is disposed of with the direction that the applicant shall surrender before the court concerned within four weeks from today and in case, a regular bail application is filed, the same be decided in view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil (supra).

7 . For the period of four weeks from today or till the time of surrender of the applicant before the court concerned, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant, in the above case.

(Justice Krishan Pahal) Order Date :- 16.1.2024 Siddhant  Yogesh Tiwari vs State Of U.P. And Another on 16 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108279395/

After arguing for some time, applicant's counsel submits that the present application for anticipatory bail may be dismissed as withdrawn with liberty to file a regular bail application which may be decided keeping in view the guidelines as laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and another, reported in 2022 SCC Online SC 825.
After hearing learned counsel for the parties, no case is made out for interference u/s 438 Cr.P.C..
The present anticipatory bail application is disposed of with the direction that the applicant shall surrender before the court concerned within four weeks from today and in case, a regular bail application is filed, the same be decided in view of the law laid down by the Supreme Court in the case of Satender Kumar Antil (supra).
7 . For the period of four weeks from today or till the time of surrender of the applicant before the court concerned, whichever is earlier, no coercive action shall be taken against the applicant, in the above case.
